judgments.author: Codex evaluation subagent
judgments.status: Provisional model-authored judgments; not independent expert ground truth.
judgments.separation: The author did not read coder implementation, development cases, or old/new coder outputs. Case content and judgments were withheld from the implementation agent until tuning was declared frozen.
judgments.goals_policy: Expected goals reflect communication outcomes requested in the brief, not every taxonomy goal associated with an expected technique.
judgments.subjects_policy: subjects lists required useful subject words; not_subjects lists particular instruction, format, or mechanism words that should not become subject searches. Other sensible subject words are not penalized by these lists.
judgments.techniques_policy: Expected techniques require a named mechanism or concrete descriptive evidence. A mood or generic style alone does not establish a mechanism. Explicitly negated techniques are excluded.

cases.text: Find visual metaphor examples about patience.
cases.rationale: The mechanism is explicitly named; patience is the concept to search for, without an additional stated communication goal.

cases.text: Use figure-ground ambiguity with birds and trees to provoke a second look.
cases.rationale: A named mechanism and explicit second-look goal should survive punctuation normalization.

cases.text: A solitary sailboat, surrounded on every side by a wide expanse of unoccupied water. The image should feel peaceful.
cases.rationale: Extensive unoccupied surroundings isolate the boat; there is no second object establishing a size comparison. Peacefulness is an explicit calm goal.

cases.text: Keep the butterfly crisp; everything behind it should dissolve into blur.
cases.rationale: Sharp subject against blurred surroundings is selective focus, not motion blur.

cases.text: An orderly row of identical chairs, except one faces the wrong direction.
cases.rationale: A regular repeated series and a single directional exception are both concretely specified. No human face or gaze is requested.

cases.text: A grand piano sitting in the middle of a supermarket aisle, as if it belongs there.
cases.rationale: The piano's placement in an ordinary supermarket is a concrete contextual mismatch. This does not establish a metaphor or mirrored composition.

cases.text: Express burnout by turning a human head into a candle burning down.
cases.rationale: Substituting a burning candle for a head transfers depletion to burnout, explicitly expressing an abstract concept.

cases.text: Guide the eye towards the cabin with leading lines, and use limited palette harmony to create calm.
cases.rationale: Two explicitly named techniques serve two explicitly named goals; neither should erase the other.

cases.text: Make the cliff look enormous beside a tiny climber. Leave almost all of the upper picture unoccupied.
cases.rationale: Two differently sized objects establish scale, while extensive unoccupied space is separately specified.

cases.text: I want a bold portrait that feels modern.
cases.rationale: Bold and modern do not specify whether colour, lighting, scale, framing, or any other particular mechanism should be used.

cases.text: Surprise viewers with a memorable bicycle image; I have not settled on a visual device.
cases.rationale: A surprise goal is explicit but the mechanism is deliberately undecided; it must not become a committed incongruity classification.

cases.text: Please avoid silhouette and motion blur. Show a horse in a field.
cases.rationale: Both named mechanisms are rejected, including the second item in the coordinated negative phrase.

cases.text: Use symmetry for the tree. Actually, avoid symmetry and use off-centre placement instead.
cases.rationale: The user explicitly retracts symmetry and names its replacement; preserving both would misread the correction.
Two subjects do not establish juxtaposition, grouping, framing, or any other particular composition.
Architecture and machinery can support many mechanisms, but these nouns alone justify none.

cases.text: Find references for a square album cover with a headline and three lines of text.
cases.rationale: These are deliverable and typography instructions, not depicted subjects or leading lines. No empty-area extent is specified, so negative-space isolation is not established.
